events.author: alexey-milovidov
events.text:
🕵 @groeneai, investigate the failure: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=126206&sha=adc31c7366d&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20(arm_binary%2C%202%2F4) and provide a fix in a separate PR. If the fix is already in progress, link it here.

`test_storage_rabbitmq/test.py::test_rabbitmq_reconnect_drops_stale_deliveries` timed out in `rabbitmqctl list_queues` (300 s). It failed on 2026-10-19 in unrelated PRs #126013 and #115849 too; this PR only changes the Arrow IPC reader.

events.author: groeneai
events.text:
No fix PR exists yet; I'm working on it and will link it here.

From the logs of all three failed runs:
- The ClickHouse side looks correct in all three: 10100 rows for 10000 messages (inside the two-block bound), no `unknown delivery tag` acks, and consumption finished about 19 s after the reconnect.
- A single `rabbitmqctl -q list_queues` poll never returned and was killed at 300 s, while the polls before it took about 0.5 s. It was a different poll each time (the 3rd, 14th and 22nd), once after the queue had already reported `0 0` twice, and in this run the container's `rabbitmq-diagnostics ping` healthcheck passed 29 times during the hang. So the broker was not stuck on the redelivered backlog; the fix belongs in the test's drain poll.

events.author: groeneai
events.text: The fix is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126746: the drain loop now asks `rabbitmqctl list_queues` only after the row count has been stable for 3 s, and a call that does not return within 30 s is abandoned and asked again under the test's own 180 s deadline. It is test-only; the ClickHouse and broker sides were healthy in all three failures.

events.author: alexey-milovidov
events.text: 🕵 Thanks, @groeneai. The only red check here is `test_storage_rabbitmq/test.py::test_rabbitmq_reconnect_drops_stale_deliveries`, and it is unrelated to this PR. Its fix is in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126746, which is still open, so I'm not merging master into this branch yet. Nothing else needs to change here.

open.title: Read Arrow structs with empty or repeated field names as unnamed Tuple

history.author: clickhouse-gh[bot]
history.text:
Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/praktika.html?PR=125674&sha=latest&name_0=PR)], commit [83e979ec]

**Summary:** ✅
- Performance Comparison: [Performance dashboard](https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/runs?q=125674)

---
#### AI Review

##### Summary

The PR reads Arrow structs with invalid field names as unnamed `Tuple` values and propagates positional matching through decoding, type hints, and dictionary uses. Reviewed head `83e979ec4491223a5196657d422c283ee3e6b003`. One previously reported correctness issue remains: case-insensitive matching can silently replace nested values with defaults.

##### Findings

**❌ Blockers**

- [`SchemaConverter.cpp:1160–1161`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/83e979ec4491223a5196657d422c283ee3e6b003/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/ArrowIPC/SchemaConverter.cpp#L1160): **Case-insensitive matching stops at unnamed tuple levels.** An Arrow column `s` of type `struct<"": struct<x: int32>>`, containing `7`, requested as `s Tuple(payload Tuple(X Int32))` with `input_format_arrow_case_insensitive_column_matching = 1`, produces `((0))` instead of `((7))`. The new unnamed outer tuple makes `alignStructFieldNamesCaseInsensitive` return at `ArrowIPCBlockInputFormat.cpp:193–194`. Subsequently, `prepareArrowColumnForCast` descends positionally through the outer tuple, matches inner `x` against `X` case-sensitively, and inserts a default at lines 349–354. Recurse positionally through unnamed tuple levels while pres [...]

history.author: clickhouse-gh[bot]
history.text:
[src/Processors/Formats/Impl/ArrowIPC/SchemaConverter.cpp:1161] [P2] Preserve case-insensitive matching inside unnamed structs

The unnamed source introduced here makes `alignStructFieldNamesCaseInsensitive` return immediately (`ArrowIPCBlockInputFormat.cpp:193–194`), so it never aligns named structs nested inside it. For example, an Arrow column `s` with type `struct<"": struct<x: int32>>` containing `7`, requested as `s Tuple(payload Tuple(X Int32))` with `input_format_arrow_case_insensitive_column_matching = 1`, is converted to `((0))` instead of `((7))`.

`prepareArrowColumnForCast` correctly descends through the outer tuple by position, but then matches the inner `x` against `X` case-sensitively and replaces the value with a default. The new type-hint handling does not prevent this later loss.

Please make `alignStructFieldNamesCaseInsensitive` recurse by position through unnamed tuple levels while preserving their unnamed type, and add a nested regression for both input formats. This is a source-level trace; the available fast-test binary does not include Arrow support.
